items.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016
items.q: And Snooky and I were together in the Clayton-Hamilton band for 26 years.

ctx.x: Okay. Because I would not have been surprised if you said the opposite.

I know. But well we were just talking about Joe Wilder. And I was introduced to him by Snooky Young. And Snooky and I were together in the Clayton-Hamilton band for 26 years. And he lived to be 90. He played until he passed away. And I just saw how young it kept him. And my dad played and it kept him young. Unless I get to where I can’t play very well you know. But I still feel like I’m really sort of — I feel like there’s a lot more music I want to write and a lot more music I want to play. And I don’t know…
Okay. You could do a Doc Cheatham.

items.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Clay Jenkins, trumpet player that plays in John Clayton‘s band.

ctx.x: Yeah, we have to leave in the morning.

You got to leave in the morning. That‘s too bad, too. Louie Bellson‘s funeral is tomorrow, I still got a chance, I might call my close friends, I called and asked them, but they… Ira Nepus is out of town with Clay Jenkins, trumpet player that plays in John Clayton‘s band. And so, he said he‘s sorry but he can‘t do it he‘s working, he‘s out of town. So I‘ll find somebody I hope. And, my daughter‘s sick, she can‘t take me, you know. She‘s got the flu, that‘s too bad too, she‘s got the flu, you know.
So when the Tonight Show Band, when Johnny left then the band ended, then that was the end of, when Johnny Carson left the Tonight Show that was it.
